2. Where the hub is implemented (file path)

Search for patterns like "SSE", "Server-Sent Events", "EventSource", "hub", "broadcast", "WebSocket", "ws", "event stream", "text/event-stream", "flush", "streaming". Look in Go files, TypeScript files, and any server code. Be very thorough - check multiple naming conventions.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

30	// userCtx returns a context that authenticates as the given user.
31	func userCtx(ctx context.Context, userID int32) context.Context {
32		return context.WithValue(ctx, auth.UserIDContextKey, userID)
33	}

35	// collectEventsFor reads events from ch for the given duration and returns them.
36	func collectEventsFor(ch <-chan []byte, d time.Duration) []string {
37		var out []string
38		deadline := time.After(d)
39		for {
40			select {
41			case data := <-ch:
42				out = append(out, string(data))
43			case <-deadline:
44				return out
45			}
46		}
47	}

51	func TestSuppressSSEContext(t *testing.T) {
52		ctx := context.Background()
53	
54		t.Run("default context is not suppressed", func(t *testing.T) {
55			assert.False(t, isSSESuppressed(ctx))
56		})
57	
58		t.Run("withSuppressSSE marks context as suppressed", func(t *testing.T) {
59			assert.True(t, isSSESuppressed(withSuppressSSE(ctx)))
60		})
61	
62		t.Run("suppression does not bleed into parent context", func(t *testing.T) {
63			suppressed := withSuppressSSE(ctx)
64			_ = suppressed

66		})
67	}

69	// ---- CreateMemoComment double-broadcast fix ----

71	func TestCreateMemoComment_NoDuplicateSSEBroadcast(t *testing.T) {
72		ctx := context.Background()
73		svc := newIntegrationService(t)
74	
75		// Create an admin so the store is initialised, then a regular commenter.
76		author, err := svc.Store.CreateUser(ctx, &store.User{
77			Username: "author", Role: store.RoleAdmin, Email: "author@example.com",
78		})
79		require.NoError(t, err)
80		commenter, err := svc.Store.CreateUser(ctx, &store.User{
81			Username: "commenter", Role: store.RoleUser, Email: "commenter@example.com",
82		})
83		require.NoError(t, err)
84	
85		authorCtx := userCtx(ctx, author.ID)
86		commenterCtx := userCtx(ctx, commenter.ID)
87	
88		// Create a public memo so the commenter can react.
89		parent, err := svc.CreateMemo(authorCtx, &v1pb.CreateMemoRequest{
90			Memo: &v1pb.Memo{Content: "parent memo", Visibility: v1pb.Visibility_PUBLIC},
91		})
92		require.NoError(t, err)
93	
94		// Subscribe after the parent memo is created so the memo.created event
95		// for the parent does not pollute the assertion window.
96		client := svc.SSEHub.Subscribe(author.ID, store.RoleAdmin)
97		defer svc.SSEHub.Unsubscribe(client)
98	
99		// Create a comment.  Before the fix, this fired both memo.created (for the
100		// comment memo) and memo.comment.created (for the parent).
101		_, err = svc.CreateMemoComment(commenterCtx, &v1pb.CreateMemoCommentRequest{
102			Name:    parent.Name,
103			Comment: &v1pb.Memo{Content: "a comment", Visibility: v1pb.Visibility_PUBLIC},
104		})
105		require.NoError(t, err)
106	
107		// Give the synchronous broadcast a moment to land in the buffer, then
108		// collect everything that arrived.
109		events := collectEventsFor(client.events, 150*time.Millisecond)
110	
111		require.Len(t, events, 1, "expected exactly one SSE event for a comment creation, got: %v", events)
112		assert.True(t, strings.Contains(events[0], `"memo.comment.created"`),
113			"expected memo.comment.created, got: %s", events[0])
114	}

## Server-Push Mechanism: SSE (Server-Sent Events)

### 1. Mechanism Used

The repository uses **SSE (Server-Sent Events)** -- not WebSocket. The server streams events over a long-lived HTTP connection with `Content-Type: text/event-stream`. Data is sent in the standard SSE wire format (`data: <JSON>\n\n`), with heartbeat comments (`: heartbeat\n\n`) every 30 seconds to keep connections alive.

### 2. Hub Implementation (Server Side)

The SSE infrastructure lives in four files under `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/`:

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go` | Core hub: defines `SSEHub` (client registry, broadcast fan-out), `SSEClient` (per-connection channel), `SSEEvent` (event payload struct), and `SSEEventType` constants. Visibility-based delivery filtering (`canReceive`) ensures private memos only reach the owner or admins. |
| `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/sse_handler.go` | HTTP handler: registers route `GET /api/v1/sse`, authenticates via Bearer token, sets SSE response headers, subscribes to the hub, and enters an event loop that writes `data:` frames and heartbeats with `Flush()`. |
| `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/sse_event_helpers.go` | Helper functions: `buildMemoName`, `resolveSSECreatorID`, `buildMemoReactionSSEEvent`. |
| `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/v1.go` | Wiring: `APIV1Service` holds the `SSEHub` field (line 36), `NewAPIV1Service` creates it via `NewSSEHub()` (line 57), and `RegisterGateway` calls `RegisterSSERoutes` (line 125). |

The hub is also referenced from the top-level server at `/bench/repo/server/server.go` (line 38, field `sseHub`), which calls `sseHub.Close()` on shutdown (line 205-206).

Tests:
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/sse_hub_test.go` -- unit tests for subscribe/unsubscribe, broadcast, private event scoping, slow client drops
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/sse_service_test.go` -- integration tests for duplicate-broadcast prevention, reaction events, attachment/relation updated events
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/test/sse_handler_test.go` -- HTTP-level tests for authentication, streaming, hub close

### 3. Frontend Client

The browser-side consumer is at `/bench/repo/web/src/hooks/useLiveMemoRefresh.ts`. It:
- Uses `fetch("/api/v1/sse")` with `Accept: text/event-stream` (not the native `EventSource` API, because it needs to send a Bearer token in the `Authorization` header)
- Reads the response body stream with `ReadableStream.getReader()` and parses the SSE wire format manually
- Implements exponential backoff reconnection (1s initial, 30s max, 2x multiplier)
- On reconnect, invalidates active React Query caches to resync
- Exposes `useSSEConnectionStatus()` for UI status indication

The hook is activated in `/bench/repo/web/src/main.tsx` (line 49) at the app root. The connection status is consumed in `/bench/repo/web/src/components/UserMenu.tsx`.

### 4. Which Memo Handlers Broadcast Through the Hub

Six SSE event types are defined (in `sse_hub.go`, lines 14-21):

| Event Type Constant | Wire Value | Broadcast Site |
